points.description: The answer conveys that the height of a tree is a length measured along a path from the root down to a leaf.
The answer conveys that the height is the longest such path, taken over all root-to-leaf paths in the tree (not just any one path).

rubric.notes: Full marks for stating that height is the length of a root-to-leaf path and that it is the longest of these paths. Equivalent wording such as 'the maximum depth of any leaf' or 'the greatest distance from the root to a leaf' earns the marks. A student who describes only a single root-to-leaf path, or only the root or leaves without a length, earns P1 at most; no credit for P2 without the idea of maximum.
